judged_text: `refreshOAuthTokens` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:16-18) returns a raw fetch `Response` in sync mode, incompatible with every consuming adapter: Google reads `res?.data` (undefined → TypeError on `token.access_token`), Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin expect axios responses (`tokenInfo.data.error` throws on undefined), Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object (undefined fields → NaN expiry persisted), Lark feeds it to `handleLarkError` which expects the `{code, msg, data}` envelope, and zoom/webex/o365/msteams parse provider-specific key names (`expires_in`, `expiry_date`) that the documented sync response never defines — the credential-sync feature cannot work against its own documented contract and several adapters hard-crash

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response` when sync mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`). Multiple consumers in this diff expect non-`Response` shapes and immediately dereference properties that won't exist on `Response`: GoogleCalendarService does `const token = res?.data` then `token.access_token` (would be `undefined` in sync mode), and Zoho CRM/Bigin both use `tokenInfo.data...` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data...` right after the call (a `Response` has no `.data`). Hubspot assigns the return value to `HubspotToken` (object expected) but would receive a `Response` in sync mode. This mismatch is directly verifiable from the new `refreshOAuthTokens` implementation and the shown call sites, and would lead to runtime errors when sync mode is active.
